data.name: Jabril
data.gender_notes: Jabril is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic word 'Jabar' which means 'strong' or 'powerful'. In Islamic tradition, Jabril is the angel who delivers the revelations of Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). The name Jabril carries the meaning “Gabriel” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Jabril usually hope their child will grow to embody gabriel and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Jabril belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gabriel.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jabril total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jabril holds significant cultural impact in the Islamic world, especially during the month of Ramadan. It is believed that this is the time when the angel Jabril increases his presence, guiding and inspiring believers during this sacred month. Further, the name Jabril is commonly associated with strength and power, reflecting the dynamic energy of this celestial being and instilling a sense of courage and inspiration in those who bear this name.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, Jabril holds great spiritual significance as the Angel Messenger of Allah. It is believed that through this divine intervention, Jabril delivers the words of God to the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), allowing the messages of the Quran to be revealed. The name Jabril reminds us of the power and presence of Allah in our lives, and inspires us to be strong in our faith and in our daily struggles. It is a reminder of the divine connection between the Creator and the created, and encourages a deep sense of submission and devotion to the will of Allah.
